gloss: to drive out, to expel, to kick out

definitions.explanation: To force someone or something to leave a place.

definitions.gloss: to kick out, to throw out
definitions.explanation: To remove someone from a position, organization, or residence, often forcibly or against their will.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}を{外|そと}に{追|お}い{出|だ}した。
{猫|ねこ}を{部屋|へや}から{追|お}い{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I chased the cat out of the room.

examples.japanese: {村人|むらびと}たちは{熊|くま}を{山|やま}の{奥|おく}へ{追|お}い{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The villagers drove the bear deep into the mountains.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{会社|かいしゃ}から{追|お}い{出|だ}された。
examples.english: He was kicked out of the company.

examples.japanese: {家賃|やちん}を{払|はら}わないと{追|お}い{出|だ}されるよ。
examples.english: If you don't pay rent, you'll be kicked out.

examples.japanese: {不正|ふせい}が{発覚|はっかく}して、{社長|しゃちょう}は{取締役会|とりしまりやくかい}から{追|お}い{出|だ}された。
examples.english: After the fraud was discovered, the president was expelled from the board of directors.

notes:
{追|お}い{出|だ}す is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) meaning to drive out or expel.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {追|お}う (to chase) + {出|だ}す (to put out) → to chase out

TRANSITIVITY:
- {追|お}い{出|だ}す ({他動詞|たどうし}): to drive someone out
- There is no common intransitive pair

ASPECT (ている):
{追|お}い{出|だ}されている indicates a state of having been expelled.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {部屋|へや}から{追|お}い{出|だ}す (drive out of a room)
- {家|いえ}から{追|お}い{出|だ}す (kick out of the house)
- {会社|かいしゃ}から{追|お}い{出|だ}す (kick out of the company)
- {国|くに}から{追|お}い{出|だ}す (expel from a country)

RELATED WORDS:
- {追放|ついほう}: exile, banishment (more formal)
- {排除|はいじょ}: exclusion, removal (formal)

[Register: Neutral]
